## Overview

The `inboggvegan` package extends `vegan` and base R (`stats::prcomp`, `stats::princomp`) multivariate analyses with customizable `ggplot2` visualizations. Because every function returns a standard `ggplot` object, plots can be styled with custom themes, scales, and facets.

```{r libraries}
library(inboggvegan)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## 1. Screeplots (`ggscreeplot`)

`ggscreeplot()` visualizes the proportion of explained variance (`"pev"`), the cumulative explained variance (`"cev"`), or `"both"` across ordination axes.

### Standard PCA (`prcomp`)

```{r scree-prcomp}
pca_arrests <- prcomp(USArrests, scale. = TRUE)
ggscreeplot(pca_arrests, type = "both") +
  ggtitle("Screeplot for USArrests PCA")
```

### Unconstrained Ordination with Broken-Stick Model (`vegan::rda`)

When working with ecological community matrices containing many species axes, use `max_axes` to focus on the leading components and `bstick = TRUE` to overlay the broken-stick null expectation:

```{r scree-vegan}
data(varespec)
data(varechem)

vare_pca <- rda(varespec, scale = TRUE)
ggscreeplot(vare_pca, type = "pev", max_axes = 10, bstick = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Lichen Pasture PCA vs. Broken-Stick Expectation")
```

## 2. Biplots for `prcomp` and `princomp` (`ggbiplot`)

`ggbiplot()` provides a fast biplot interface for `stats::prcomp()` and `stats::princomp()` objects, supporting custom axis choices, observation coloring, and jittering:

```{r biplot-prcomp}
pca_iris <- prcomp(iris[, 1:4], scale. = TRUE)

ggbiplot(
  pca_iris,
  choices = c(1, 2),
  colordata = iris[, "Species", drop = FALSE],
  pch = 16
) +
  ggtitle("Iris PCA Biplot (Axes 1 & 2)")
```

You can also inspect higher axes (e.g., PC1 vs. PC3) or switch from points (`type = "p"`) to text labels (`type = "t"`):

```{r biplot-prcomp-13}
ggbiplot(
  pca_iris,
  choices = c(1, 3),
  colordata = iris[, "Species", drop = FALSE],
  type = "t"
) +
  ggtitle("Iris PCA Biplot (Axes 1 & 3)")
```

## 3. Extended `vegan` Biplots (`ggbiplot_vegan`)

`ggbiplot_vegan()` is the core workhorse for `rda`, `cca`, and `capscale` ordinations. It supports independent control over sites, species vectors, correlation circles, group centroids, confidence ellipses, continuous environmental vectors (`bp`), and discrete factor centroids (`cn`).

### Unconstrained PCA with Correlation Circle

When `scaling = 2` (species scaling), angles between species arrows reflect their correlations, and species approaching the correlation circle radius (`cor_circle_geom = "line"`) are best represented by the plotted plane:

```{r biplot-vegan-unconstrained}
ggbiplot_vegan(
  vare_pca,
  scaling = 2,
  species_abbrev = TRUE,
  cor_circle_geom = "line"
) +
  ggtitle("Unconstrained RDA with Correlation Circle (Scaling = 2)")
```

### Constrained RDA with Continuous Environmental Gradients

Here we constrain `varespec` by soil nitrogen (`N`), phosphorus (`P`), and potassium (`K`), while coloring sites along the continuous `pH` gradient:

```{r biplot-vegan-constrained-cont}
vare_rda <- rda(varespec ~ N + P + K, data = varechem)

ggbiplot_vegan(
  vare_rda,
  site_data = varechem,
  site_mapping = aes(color = pH),
  species_geom = "text",
  species_abbrev = TRUE,
  bp_geom = "arrow"
) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  ggtitle("Constrained RDA with Environmental Vectors (N, P, K) and Site pH")
```

### Constrained CCA with Factor Centroids, Group Ellipses & Centroids

Using the classic `dune` meadow dataset, we can combine continuous constraints (`A1` horizon thickness) and categorical management types (`Management`), adding 68% probability ellipses around site groups:

```{r biplot-vegan-cca}
data(dune)
data(dune.env)

dune_cca <- cca(dune ~ A1 + Management, data = dune.env)

ggbiplot_vegan(
  dune_cca,
  site_data = dune.env,
  site_merge_by = "row.numbers",
  site_mapping = aes(color = Management, shape = Management),
  ellipse_geom = "line",
  ellipse_mapping = aes(color = Management),
  ellipse_level = 0.68,
  species_geom = "point",
  species_mapping = NULL,
  bp_geom = "arrow",
  cn_geom = "text"
) +
  ggtitle("Constrained CCA of Dune Meadow Vegetation")
```

## 4. Custom Layer Construction with `get_display_data()` and Geoms

If you want complete manual control over a `ggplot2` pipeline, extract tidy coordinate data frames using `get_display_data()` and layer `geom_arrow()`, `geom_arrowlabel()`, `geom_corcircle()`, and `stat_centroid()` directly:

```{r manual-layers}
site_df <- get_display_data(
  vare_pca,
  data = varechem,
  display = "sites",
  scaling = 2,
  merge_by = "row.names"
)
species_df <- get_display_data(
  vare_pca,
  display = "species",
  scaling = 2,
  species_abbrev = TRUE
)
circle_r <- attr(species_df, "r")
axis_labs <- attr(site_df, "axis.labels")

ggplot(site_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  geom_corcircle(radius = circle_r, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_arrow(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2),
             data = species_df,
             color = "firebrick", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_arrowlabel(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = Row.names),
                  data = species_df, color = "firebrick", size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Humdepth, color = Baresoil)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = axis_labs[1], y = axis_labs[2], title = "Custom Multi-Layer Biplot")
```

## 5. Additional Community Ecology Visualizations

### Convex Hulls and Spider Diagrams (`ggordihull_spider`)

Ideal for visualizing group dispersion in NMDS (`metaMDS`), PCA, or PCoA space alongside PERMANOVA (`adonis2`) analyses:

```{r hull-spider}
set.seed(42)
dune_nmds <- metaMDS(dune, trace = FALSE)

ggordihull_spider(
  dune_nmds,
  groups = "Management",
  site_data = dune.env,
  show_hull = TRUE,
  show_spider = TRUE,
  show_centroids = TRUE
) +
  ggtitle("NMDS Ordination with Management Hulls and Spider Webs")
```

### Smooth Environmental Surfaces (`ggordisurf`)

When environmental gradients respond non-linearly across ordination space, `ggordisurf()` fits a 2D GAM smooth via `vegan::ordisurf()` and overlays labeled contour lines:

```{r ordisurf}
ggordisurf(dune_nmds, env_var = "A1", site_data = dune.env) +
  ggtitle("NMDS with GAM Smooth Surface for A1 Horizon Thickness")
```

### Post-Hoc Environmental Vector Fitting (`ggenvfit`)

Fit environmental vectors and factor centroids onto an unconstrained ordination and automatically filter by permutation $p$-value (`p.max = 0.05`):

```{r envfit}
ggenvfit(
  dune_nmds,
  env = dune.env[, c("A1", "Moisture", "Management")],
  p.max = 0.05,
  permutations = 499
) +
  ggtitle("Significant Environmental Vectors and Factors (p <= 0.05)")
```

### NMDS Shepard Stress Diagram (`ggshepard`)

Assess goodness-of-fit for NMDS ordinations by plotting ordination distances against observed community dissimilarities:

```{r shepard}
ggshepard(dune_nmds) +
  ggtitle("Shepard Diagram for Dune NMDS")
```
